mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps in two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations spike (>4% YoY).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above trend within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost margins, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not accelerate above 3.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the decline reverses within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% YoY, sustained for two months, signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY growth > 10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or housing starts decline in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages indicates a labor market expansion with slack, which supports corporate hiring and productivity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or either series reverts below its 12-month average within the week.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue prospects for consumer-facing sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong export growth.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >0.5% for 4 consecutive months AND export growth is not above 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or RSAFS rebounds by more than 1% in the fifth month.
